title: Memory management in depth: stack, heap and the collector

videos.script: The go course showed where a value lives and how the collector frees it. This lesson takes the lid off, and measures what each part costs. {{stacks}} First the stacks. Every goroutine has one, and it starts at two kilobytes. Watch one grow to thirty-two megabytes, move to a new address, and shrink back. {{colours}} Then the collector itself. It marks your heap while your program keeps changing it. Three colours and a write barrier are how it never loses a live value. You will read every field of its trace on the hits program. {{knobs}} Next, the two settings everybody reaches for. GOGC and GOMEMLIMIT, measured on a program that keeps two million log lines in memory. One limit makes it run at half speed, and you will see why. {{allocs}} Last, allocations. Three tools count them, from the whole process down to one line of code. Three techniques remove them: preallocating, reusing a buffer, and a pool. Each one is measured before and after. By the end, you can say where a Go program's memory goes, and which change would actually help.
